cause: A stale compliance policy reference remained attached during Intune compliance evaluation, so the current encryption state was not read correctly and devices were assessed against an older policy revision, producing the EncryptionMissing result and stale noncompliant status.

title: Internal DNS names failing to resolve from corporate resolver
description: Internal users and dependent services across the Denver office were trying to resolve hostnames under corp.local through the corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local, 10.20.1.10), but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or outdated A records instead of the current internal addresses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Ellison (EMP-40821) from the infrastructure team, who noticed that internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local were unreachable by name from his workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME (10.20.44.87). Several other users including Priya Nagarajan also confirmed intermittent failures from their machines.
cause: Corporate DNS resolver cache contained stale internal A records and continued serving outdated answers after authoritative corp.local zone records had been updated.
fixed_by: Flushed the stale cache entries on the primary corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) using rndc flush to remove outdated A records (e.g., 10.10.10.5) being returned for affected corp.local hosts including internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local.

title: Intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal host 'app-db.internal' from one client subnet
description: Users on client subnet 10.20.30.0/24 (primarily the finance team in the Columbus office) were trying to resolve the internal database host app-db.internal, but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN while the same name resolved successfully from other subnets. The issue was originally reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@corplabs.com, emp ID FIN-40821) who noticed her application dashboard could not reach the internal database dependency by hostname in corp-datacenter-1. No recent DNS record change was logged, and Maria did not have access to internal DNS zone data or resolver configuration, so resolver path and forwarding behavior required verification by the network team.
cause: Subnet-specific DNS resolution was caused by an affected resolver path for clients on 10.20.30.0/24 that had incorrect or stale conditional forwarding/cache data for the internal zone. This caused that resolver to return NXDOMAIN for app-db.internal while other resolver paths continued to return the correct internal record.
fixed_by: Identify the resolver serving clients on 10.20.30.0/24 — confirmed as dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal (10.20.30.2) — and compare its response for app-db.internal against a known-good internal resolver (dns-res-core-01.corplabs.internal, 10.50.1.10). NXDOMAIN was returned only by dns-res-east-02.

title: Internal hostname fails to resolve — stale A record in internal DNS
description: Multiple internal users and monitoring agents were trying to reach app.example.internal, but name resolution intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or the outdated IP address 10.20.5.47 from internal DNS. title: Intermittent internal DNS resolution failures for app.payments.corp

cause: DNS maintenance left inconsistent internal resolver state for the app.payments.corp zone path, with stale or incorrect cached data and/or forwarder handling causing intermittent negative responses and timeouts despite the zone record needing to resolve internally. The incident behavior across multiple hosts and regions points to resolver-side cache/forwarder inconsistency rather than a single client issue.

title: Internal hostname resolution failing via internal DNS resolver
description: Internal services were trying to resolve service-internal.company.local through the primary internal DNS resolver at 10.10.0.5 (DNS-RESV-01.infra.company.local) in the Newark datacenter, but the resolver intermittently returned NXDOMAIN while direct queries to the authoritative internal DNS server at 10.10.0.12 (DNS-AUTH-01.infra.company.local) returned the correct A record (10.20.5.44). This was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, employee ID E-40821) from the platform engineering team after the internal-api-gateway on host APPGW-PROD-02 began logging connection failures to service-internal.company.local. The issue prevented internal APIs that rely on name-based routing from reaching the internal endpoint by hostname and caused inconsistent application connectivity across the on-premises environment, affecting multiple downstream consumers.
cause: One internal DNS resolver was missing the required conditional forwarder for the internal zone, causing some queries for service-internal.company.local to be routed incorrectly. The resolver then cached the negative response, so it continued serving stale NXDOMAIN answers even though the authoritative internal DNS server had the correct A record.
fixed_by: Added the missing conditional forwarder for the internal company.local zone on the affected resolver DNS-RESV-01 at 10.10.0.5, pointing to the authoritative server DNS-AUTH-01 at 10.10.0.12, so requests are consistently sent to the correct authoritative internal DNS path. Change performed by Priya Nair (pnair).

title: Intermittent internal DNS resolution failures for internal services
description: Internal services intermittently fail to resolve internal hostnames needed by the HR Portal (hrportal.corp.eastnet.local), Payroll API (payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local), and Internal Inventory Service (inventory.corp.eastnet.local) in the on-premises us-east-1 environment at the Newark data center. The reporter did not provide a complete hostname list or precise failure timestamps, which limited scope validation.
cause: Intermittent resolution was most consistent with inconsistent internal DNS pathing: one or more resolvers had stale cached records while conditional forwarding or zone delegation for the affected internal zone was not consistently returning authoritative answers. This caused different resolvers to return NXDOMAIN, timeouts, or outdated addresses for the same hostname until cache and forwarder configuration were corrected.
fixed_by: Reviewed the affected internal DNS zone records on DNS-AUTH-EAST-01 for the corp.eastnet.local zone, validated current A records (hrportal → 10.40.5.33, payroll-api → 10.40.5.41, inventory → 10.40.5.52) and TTL values (300s), and corrected stale record data where resolver responses did not match the authoritative zone.

fixed_by: Reviewed the internal DNS zone corp.internal for svc-inventory.corp and corrected the A record so it pointed to the current service IP 10.42.16.55 instead of the decommissioned host reference 10.42.16.12.

cause: bind-resolver-01 was serving stale cached DNS data for corp.local due to an outdated DNS update policy reference and cache entries that were not invalidated after the authoritative record changed, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN and old A record responses despite the authoritative zone being correct.
fixed_by: Verified the authoritative corp.local zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local contained the correct A record (10.50.12.88) for service1.corp.local and corrected the record where needed so the source of truth matched the intended service IP.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for internal-service.local

title: Intermittent DNS resolution for internal-service.example.com
description: Users and monitoring systems across multiple offices were trying to resolve internal-service.example.com for access to the internal-service endpoint, but DNS responses were intermittent across locations. cause: Stale cached A record data on downstream/internal resolvers and conditional forwarding path inconsistency caused some clients to receive the previous address 10.1.2.45 after the authoritative zone had already been updated to 10.2.3.50.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failure for AppTeam
description: AppTeam engineer Priya Nair (emp ID: E-40291) reported that two application hosts (APPNODE-PRD-01 and APPNODE-PRD-02) in the corp-datacenter-1 on-prem environment at the Phoenix facility were unable to reliably reach the internal API endpoint api.internal.corp. title: Internal hostname service.example.local intermittent DNS failures — resolved

description: Multiple internal users and application monitoring were trying to reach services by hostname under corp.internal, but internal names were returning NXDOMAIN from the primary resolver (DNS-RESOLVER-01.corp.internal, 10.40.2.10). The affected application, internal-service-app, could not make name-based connections to internal endpoints such as api-gateway.corp.internal and inventory-svc.corp.internal, creating a service interruption for users in the on-prem us-east-dc1 environment. The issue was initially reported by Maria Sandoval (emp ID E-40821) from the Arlington office via the Network Operations bridge call, and was corroborated by automated alerts from Network Monitoring at 22:44 UTC.
cause: Conditional forwarder for the internal zone corp.internal was missing on the primary and secondary DNS resolvers, causing queries to return NXDOMAIN and leaving stale negative cache entries for affected names.
fixed_by: Added the missing conditional forwarder for the corp.internal zone on the primary DNS resolver (DNS-RESOLVER-01.corp.internal, 10.40.2.10) pointing to DNSAUTH-INT-01.corp.internal (10.40.1.5) and validated the target forwarding path with dig queries.

title: Internal hostname resolution failing
description: The inventory-service running on internal app hosts (including APPHOST-LNX-04 and APPHOST-LNX-05 in the Austin datacenter) could not connect to db01.corp.local because internal DNS resolution was failing. Affected hosts returned NXDOMAIN for the hostname and some hosts saw intermittent DNS timeouts, blocking database connectivity for the service in corp-datacenter-1. The issue was initially reported by DevOps engineer Priya Nambiar (pnambiar, emp ID DVP-2294) who noticed inventory-service health checks failing at approximately 15:50 UTC. Investigation focused on the internal DNS zone and resolver cache path for the corporate .local namespace.
cause: Internal DNS was serving stale data because db01.corp.local had an out-of-sync A record in the internal zone and stale negative cache entries on the DNS resolver tier, causing NXDOMAIN responses and intermittent lookup failures from app hosts.
fixed_by: Validated the authoritative internal DNS zone entry for db01.corp.local and corrected the A record from the stale address 10.40.5.20 to the current database server IP address 10.40.5.35, as confirmed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) from the network infrastructure team.

title: Internal DNS resolver serving stale A record causing hostname resolution failures
description: Internal users in the Portland office and the finance-api application (running on host FINAPI-PROD-01) were trying to reach internal-service.corp.local, but name resolution intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or an outdated IP (10.10.5.21) while direct access by the current IP 10.10.8.33 still worked. The issue was first reported by developer Marcus Jennings (mjennings, emp ID EMP-40821) and affected automated CI/CD jobs as well as interactive API access after a DNS zone update performed on 2026-01-12. Symptoms indicated inconsistent data between the authoritative zone on ns1.corp.local and the internal resolver cache on dns-resolver-west.corp.local.
cause: Internal DNS resolvers retained stale cached data for internal-service.corp.local after the zone record changed, causing intermittent responses with an old A record or lookup failures until caches were refreshed.
fixed_by: Corrected the A record for internal-service.corp.local in the internal authoritative DNS zone on ns1.corp.local to 10.10.8.33 and incremented the zone serial to 2026011201 so downstream resolvers could detect the update. Change performed by Priya Nair (pnair) and verified via zone transfer to ns2.corp.local.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for api.internal.company.local
description: Internal developers on the DevOps and Platform Engineering teams are intermittently unable to resolve api.internal.company.local from corporate network locations, which prevents the internal-api/service-discovery workflow from reaching the endpoint by name. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) from the Austin office, and subsequently confirmed by additional developers in the Chicago and Portland offices. Affected users see NXDOMAIN or timeouts when querying corporate DNS resolvers (e.g., from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD at 10.42.17.88), while a public resolver (8.8.8.8) returns a valid address for the same hostname. Scope appears limited to corporate DNS pathing or internal zone handling rather than a full service outage, and no recent zone edits or resolver cache evidence were initially attached.
cause: Corporate DNS resolution for api.internal.company.local was intermittently failing because the internal zone/conditional forwarding path was not consistently returning the authoritative record across corporate resolvers, leading some resolvers to answer NXDOMAIN from stale or incorrect cache/forwarding state while public lookup still returned an address.
fixed_by: Validated the authoritative A record for api.internal.company.local in the intended internal DNS zone (company.local) and corrected the record TTL to the current expected value of 300 seconds, confirming the record pointed to 10.200.5.34.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal service
description: Engineering users and internal application teams were trying to reach internal-service1 at service1.company.local from on-premises Linux hosts in the private us-east-1 data center (Ashburn facility). It affected internal-service1 and internal-frontend, blocked application connectivity by hostname, and coincided with resolver latency spikes and cache inconsistencies after a recent DNS zone update performed earlier that morning.
cause: The internal DNS resolver served a stale cached A record for service1.company.local after a recent zone update, causing intermittent mismatches between resolver cache contents and the current internal zone data and resulting in NXDOMAIN responses and lookup timeouts until the cache was flushed.
fixed_by: Reviewed the authoritative internal DNS zone for service1.company.local, corrected the A record to match the current endpoint address (10.42.18.61), and confirmed the zone data reflected the intended value. Raj Kapoor (rkapoor) performed the verification against the zone file on the authoritative server.

title: Internal hostname resolving to stale address from DNS resolver
description: Multiple internal users in the Austin office were trying to reach service.internal.example.com from the internal application path, but the hostname resolved to an outdated IP address (172.16.10.45) instead of the current internal service endpoint (172.16.10.78). cause: Internal DNS resolver cache retained and served a stale A record for service.internal.example.com (172.16.10.45) instead of the authoritative current address (172.16.10.78).
fixed_by: Queried service.internal.example.com on the internal resolver dns-resolver-01.corp.internal from client WORKSTATION-PC-RN (10.42.16.93, Rachel Nguyen) and confirmed it was returning the stale cached A record 172.16.10.45 rather than the current authoritative address.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failing for api.internal.corp
description: Internal users and monitoring were trying to reach the service at api.internal.corp, but name resolution intermittently returned a stale A record (10.40.2.15) instead of the current service IP (10.40.5.80). cause: A stale cached A record remained on one or more internal recursive resolvers/forwarders after the DNS record change, so clients querying different resolver paths intermittently received the previous IP even though the authoritative zone had the updated address.
fixed_by: Queried api.internal.corp against the authoritative DNS server (AUTH-DNS-01) and internal recursive resolvers (RSLV-INT-02, RSLV-INT-03) to confirm the authoritative zone served the new IP (10.40.5.80) while some resolver paths—particularly RSLV-INT-03 in Portland—still returned the previous address (10.40.2.15).

title: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed
description: A managed Windows 10 21H2 corporate laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, asset tag ENG-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID E-20487) in the Portland office was reported as noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune. Authentication appeared to succeed briefly—users saw the 'Connected' status for 2–3 seconds—then the session was reset and internal CRM, Confluence, and other SAML-protected internal apps remained unreachable. The issue was first reported at approximately 06:10 UTC by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) from the Sales team and quickly confirmed by additional users including Marcus Delgado (Engineering). The issue began this morning following the routine certificate rotation window (scheduled 2026-04-13 22:00–02:00 UTC) and affected multiple users globally across both macOS 14.4 and Windows 11 23H2 endpoints.
cause: Affected endpoints were presenting expired device certificates to the GlobalProtect gateway after successful Okta MFA, causing the gateway to terminate the VPN session immediately after authentication.
fixed_by: Generated and deployed renewed device certificates to affected managed endpoints (including WORKSTATION-MACBOOK-RN for rnguyen and WORKSTATION-PC-MD for mdelgado) through the Device Certificate Service, issuing new certs from the CorpLabs Device CA with a validity period through 2027-04-14.

The issue was escalated by the Charlotte site lead, Derek Whitfield (derek.whitfield@corplabs.com).
cause: The Wireless Controller's RADIUS server certificate expired at 2026-04-24T02:00Z, causing 802.1X EAP authentication failures and preventing many clients from completing wireless authentication and DHCP access on the corporate Wi-Fi network.
fixed_by: Reissued and installed a new valid RADIUS certificate (CN=radius01.corp.eastnet.local, valid through 2027-04-24) on the Cisco Wireless Controller WLC-EAST-01 for 802.1X authentication, coordinated by network engineer Marcus Jennings (mjennings).

title: Unable to connect to Corporate Wi-Fi (expired certificate) — partial workaround applied
description: Multiple employees on managed Windows and macOS devices in the Austin office were unable to connect to the Corporate Wi-Fi (Corp-Employees SSID) after the overnight certificate rollover on 2026-04-25. title: unable to connect to Corporate Wi‑Fi — EAP-TLS authentication failing

title: Reopened: Device cannot access Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple users in the London office were trying to reconnect managed laptops and BYOD devices to Corporate Wi-Fi after a recent wireless certificate renewal. The issue was initially reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) and confirmed by several colleagues on the 4th floor. Devices failed 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication and showed messages such as "EAP-TLS certificate expired," "Supplicant: certificate verification failed," or "No network access after joining." Rachel's laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) at IP 10.42.16.88 was among the first to fail. The issue began after the certificate was renewed on the primary controller (WLC-LON-PRIMARY), where some endpoints temporarily recovered, but additional devices failed the next morning due to incomplete certificate propagation to secondary nodes (WLC-LON-SEC02, WLC-LON-SEC03) and stale local Wi-Fi profiles, blocking normal network access for the affected user group.
cause: The renewed EAP-TLS certificate chain was not fully propagated across all wireless controller cluster nodes after the initial renewal, so some authentication paths still presented or validated against the expired certificate state. Affected endpoints also retained stale or corrupt Corporate Wi-Fi profiles, causing continued certificate validation failures even after the primary controller was updated.
fixed_by: Validated the renewed wireless certificate chain on the primary controller WLC-LON-PRIMARY and confirmed the correct server certificate (CN=wifi.corplabs.com, issued 2026-04-26) and trust chain were present for EAP-TLS authentication. Verification performed by Carlos Mendes (c.mendes).

title: Corporate Wi-Fi: Devices show 'No network access'
description: Users in the London office were able to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpWiFi-5G) and complete 802.1X authentication via ClearPass NAC, but devices then showed "No network access" and could not reach internal resources. The issue started after an overnight configuration push at approximately 02:30 UTC on 2026-04-27 and affected both laptops and mobile devices across floors 3–5 of the London building. Staff member Rachel Nguyen (emp ID EMP-40821) first reported the problem at 08:15 local time, and multiple other users including contractor David Kowalski confirmed the same symptoms. The issue blocked normal corporate network access for staff and contractors, preventing access to intranet portals and shared drives.
cause: An incorrect AD group-to-NAC policy mapping introduced during the overnight configuration push assigned valid authenticated users to the Quarantined access role instead of the normal corporate access policy.
fixed_by: Reviewed ClearPass/NAC and wireless controller policy decisions to confirm authenticated users were being mapped to the Quarantined role because of an incorrect AD group association. Network engineer James Thornton (j.thornton, EMP-55193) examined the ClearPass Access Tracker entries for users r.nguyen, d.kowalski, and p.mehta, verifying that the enforcement profile 'Quarantine-Restricted' was incorrectly applied following change CHG-88214.

title: Multiple users cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi

Some endpoints also retained stale or corrupt Wi-Fi profiles after certificate renewal, requiring local profile remediation.
fixed_by: Generated or imported a renewed wireless server certificate and deployed it to the Wireless Controller (WLC-BLDG4-01.corp.local) for EAP-TLS authentication. Deployment was coordinated by network engineer Kevin Marsh (kmarsh).

title: Users unable to join Corporate Wi‑Fi - authentication failures
description: Multiple Sales users in the Dallas office were trying to connect managed Windows, macOS, and iOS devices to the corporate SSID 'CorpWiFi' but were unable to complete network access starting around 07:45 CDT this morning. Work performed by network engineer Raj Patel (rpatel, EMP-51209).

title: Users unable to join Corporate Wi‑Fi
description: Multiple corporate staff at the Frankfurt office were trying to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-5G) on managed devices starting around 06:30 UTC. 802.1X authentication via EAP-TLS completed successfully, but affected endpoints were immediately placed into NAC quarantine or showed limited connectivity with repeated disconnects. Users such as Elena Richter (e.richter@corplabs.com) and Markus Hahn reported they could associate to the SSID but could not obtain normal network access needed for routine work. Initial reports were gathered by service desk analyst Priya Nair (EMP-40821). Evidence from ClearPass Policy Manager (cppm-emea-01.corplabs.internal) and the wireless controller (WLC-FRA-02) pointed to a policy assignment mismatch affecting the Corporate device group rather than a credential failure.
cause: ClearPass NAC policy assignment for the Corporate device group was misconfigured, causing successfully authenticated endpoints to be evaluated against a deny/quarantine policy instead of the intended allow policy.
fixed_by: Updated the ClearPass enforcement and role-mapping policy on cppm-emea-01.corplabs.internal so the Corporate device group (Role: Corp-Managed) matched the correct Corp-Allow enforcement profile instead of the Quarantine-Deny policy after successful 802.1X EAP-TLS authentication. Change performed by Anil Kapoor (akapoor, EMP-60193).

title: Unable to connect to Corporate Wi-Fi — EAP-TLS authentication failures
description: Multiple users in the New York office were trying to join the Corporate Wi-Fi (CorpWiFi) from managed laptops, but authentication failed or devices repeatedly disconnected after association. The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40291) from the Sales team, who noticed her laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG could not connect after returning from a meeting. Several endpoints displayed "EAP-TLS: certificate expired" during 802.1X login against RADIUS server 10.40.12.5. The issue started immediately after the scheduled certificate rotation maintenance window on 2026-05-04 and blocked normal corporate wireless access across affected SSIDs for the NY Office / Sales user group.
cause: The RADIUS/Wireless Controller server certificate used for 802.1X EAP-TLS authentication expired during the certificate rotation window, causing clients to reject the authentication server and fail wireless login.
fixed_by: Validated that the active RADIUS/Wireless Controller certificate (CN=radius.corplabs.internal, serial 4A:7C:0E:91) presented during EAP-TLS authentication was expired as of 2026-05-04T23:59:59Z and confirmed it matched the controller (WLC-NY-01) and RADIUS (10.40.12.5) failure logs reviewed by Nathan Williams (nwilliams).

title: Users unable to connect to Corporate Wi‑Fi
description: Employees across the Arlington corporate office were unable to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) using 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) at approximately 06:45 UTC on 2026-05-05. Client devices showed certificate-related authentication failures — specifically 'certificate expired' and 'secure connection failed' prompts — and users were left without network access after attempting to connect. The problem affected broad office connectivity across floors 2–5 until wireless authentication certificates issued by the internal CA (ca-pki.corplabs.internal) were renewed and controller profiles corrected.
cause: The certificate used for wireless 802.1X authentication had expired, causing TLS validation failures between the wireless infrastructure and RADIUS authentication flow and blocking EAP-TLS authentication for Corporate Wi-Fi clients.
fixed_by: Confirmed the expired certificate (CN=wifi-auth.corplabs.internal, expired 2026-05-04T23:59:59Z) in the wireless authentication path on radius01.corplabs.internal and installed a valid signed replacement certificate issued by ca-pki.corplabs.internal to restore successful 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication. Initial temporary certificate applied by Raj Patel (rpatel) at 07:32 UTC.

title: cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: I was trying to connect my Windows 10 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-SALES-MK) to Corporate Wi-Fi in the Frankfurt office but the device joined the CorpWiFi-5G SSID and then immediately showed "No network access" after 802.1X authentication. My username is mkowalski and my employee ID is EMP-40821. The issue recurred the day after a prior wireless certificate renewal (handled by network support agent Priya Nair) that had only restored service temporarily. Restarting the laptop and forgetting and rejoining the SSID did not resolve the problem, leaving me unable to use corporate wireless access for normal work. I can be reached at mkowalski@corplabs.com or +49 170 5529183 if further details are needed.
cause: Corrupted or stale corporate Wi-Fi profile on the endpoint caused inconsistent 802.1X authentication state and improper NAC policy assignment after certificate renewal.
fixed_by: Removed the existing Corporate Wi-Fi profile and deleted saved wireless credentials from the affected Windows 10 laptop LAPTOP-SALES-MK (user mkowalski, EMP-40821) to clear the corrupted 802.1X configuration.

title: Device joins Corporate Wi-Fi but receives no network access
description: I'm using a Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK, IP 10.42.17.89) in the Newark office, US-East Engineering. After joining the Corp-WiFi SSID this morning, my device showed "Connected, no internet" and I could not reach any internal resources (e.g., SharePoint, Jira) or external sites. The connection also intermittently dropped and reconnected on its own. This started after the wireless controller certificate refresh/update performed earlier today by the network team. My employee ID is E-20841 and my username is mkim. The issue completely blocked my normal corporate network access over Wi-Fi.
cause: Expired EAP certificate on the Wireless Controller caused 802.1X post-auth validation failures, which prevented successful NAC/DHCP completion after SSID association.
fixed_by: Reviewed wireless controller (WLC-EAST-02.corplabs.internal) and NAC authentication logs to confirm that client WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK (user mkim, MAC F4:8C:50:1A:3E:77) was associating to Corp-WiFi but failing post-auth 802.1X EAP-TLS certificate validation and not receiving a DHCP lease from the 10.42.16.0/22 Engineering VLAN pool.

title: Multiple users cannot join Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple employees across two floors in the US-East HQ could not join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID using the managed 802.1X/EAP-TLS wireless profile on Windows laptops and macOS devices. Affected users include Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) from Engineering and Derek Kowalski (EMP-51093) from Sales, among others. Connection attempts failed during certificate-based authentication, NAC denied access, and users were left without normal corporate network connectivity for business work until guest Wi-Fi or hotspot workarounds were used. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen via the local helpdesk at approximately 05:50 UTC.
cause: Expired EAP-TLS server certificate on the wireless authentication path caused client trust validation failures during 802.1X authentication, and NAC subsequently denied access for affected sessions.
fixed_by: Renew the expired EAP-TLS server certificate (expired 2026-05-05T23:59:00Z) from the internal CA and deploy the updated certificate and full trust chain to the RADIUS servers handling Corporate Wi-Fi authentication. Certificate renewal coordinated by Nathan Williams (nwilliams@corplabs.com).

title: Software Center installation blocked for FinanceApp (entitlement missing) — resolved
description: Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40218) on managed corporate Windows device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN reported that FinanceApp v4.2.1 could not be installed from Software Center. The application was not appearing in the catalog for rachel.nguyen even after a manual sync and machine policy retrieval cycle, and when Rachel tried running an approved installer package separately via the Software Center available deployments link, the install did not complete — returning an entitlement authorization error. The missing software was preventing Rachel from accessing required finance workflows ahead of the Q2 close deadline. Device IP at time of report: 10.22.47.115.
cause: FinanceApp deployment targeting is misconfigured or not being processed correctly in the endpoint management platform despite valid entitlement membership.
fixed_by: Validated that the affected user rachel.nguyen (EMP-40218) and device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN were correctly synchronized in the FIN-FinanceApp-Entitlement Azure AD group and that no local Endpoint Protection or application control policy was blocking the FinanceApp installer.

title: Software Center installation blocked by Endpoint Protection (resolved)
description: I (Rachel Nguyen, emp ID EMP-40821) on a corporate Windows laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN, IP 10.42.17.88) reported that FinanceApp was available through approved channels but installation attempts were being stopped on the device. The application was needed for business use, and Software Center behavior was inconsistent during troubleshooting, with the main I impact being inability to complete the install. title: Account locked again after password reset

title: account locked after failed sign-ins
description: I changed my corporate password through the Password Reset Portal on May 7th but continued to receive account lockouts when trying to access Corporate SSO (https://sso.corplabs.com) and OWA mailbox services. My username is mreeves and the lockouts started almost immediately after the reset completed. The repeated lockouts are blocking access to corporate applications and require further investigation beyond a standard password reset. I'm based in the Charlotte office and need this resolved before a client meeting tomorrow.
cause: A non-mobile service, legacy client, or integrated application continued using outdated stored credentials after the password reset, repeatedly triggering Active Directory lockouts.

title: Laptop slow
description: I am reporting that my corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LP-MREEVES, IP 10.42.17.83) becomes very slow immediately after login, with desktop interaction delayed and common applications such as Outlook, Edge, and internal tools taking 20-60 seconds to respond. My user account is mreeves (employee ID EMP-209415) and I am based in the Charlotte office on the Sales floor. The issue affects normal post-login work on the endpoint and appears to occur during the startup window, but the exact trigger is not obvious from my report.
cause: A recently applied endpoint configuration introduced resource-heavy post-login startup processing that kept CPU and memory utilization elevated and delayed application launches.
fixed_by: Reviewed the newly applied startup-related policy set ('Sales-Startup-Hardening-2026Q2') on WORKSTATION-LP-MREEVES for user mreeves and identified the task or setting adding excessive post-login workload, specifically a redundant inventory collection and compliance scan triggered at each login.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Remote users on managed Windows 10 laptops in the Frankfurt office were trying to connect to the corporate network through GlobalProtect while working remotely. Users including Elena Vasquez (emp ID: EMP-90274) and Marco Bellini reported that after approving the Okta MFA prompt, GlobalProtect showed connected only briefly and then dropped the session before internal applications such as the intranet and Confluence became usable. The issue was first reported by Elena from her device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-EV (IP 192.168.14.37) and was reproducible on multiple reconnect attempts. It was affecting devices in the Sales and Marketing group that had recently received a VPN profile update pushed on 2026-05-06.
cause: GlobalProtect profile misconfiguration on affected endpoints caused the client to use a certificate mapping that did not match the active enrolled device certificate, triggering post-auth policy disconnects after successful Okta MFA.
fixed_by: Corrected the GlobalProtect profile configuration on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-EV and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MB so the active profile referenced the currently enrolled device certificate (thumbprint 8A:3F:…:D1) issued by the Device Certificate Service, replacing the stale reference to 2C:7B:…:E4.

title: Print Server jobs stuck
description: Users in multiple departments at the Columbus office reported that documents sent to the shared HP LaserJet MFP on PS-PRINT01 were not printing reliably. The initial report was filed by Maria Gonzalez (emp ID E-40821) from the Finance group, noting that print jobs submitted from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG remained stuck at 0% in the queue for over 30 minutes. The printer queue on PS-PRINT01 remained available, but some submitted jobs stalled and others delayed for extended periods, disrupting routine office printing across at least three floors. Initial reports referenced driver or spooler issues, but current checks did not show a consistent driver failure on the print server. Additional users including Derek Huang and Priya Nair confirmed similar behavior from their machines.
cause: Intermittent print job processing failure not explained by queue state or driver version; likely related to specific document rendering or downstream printer handling, requiring further vendor or platform escalation.
fixed_by: Capture failing sample job characteristics, including document type, size, application source, and exact time submitted through PS-PRINT01. Specifically collect the stalled jobs from mgonzalez (Q2_Finance_Report.xlsx, submitted 15:18 UTC) and dhuang (48-page PDF submitted 15:22 UTC from WORKSTATION-PC-DH) as representative failure samples.

title: Print jobs stuck on Print Server PDQ-Print01
description: Multiple users in the Philadelphia office reported that printing to the shared HP LaserJet MFP M634 through PS-PRINT01 stopped working after recent maintenance changes on the print server. Submitted jobs from users including Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40821) and David Chen (dchen) remained pending in the shared queue \\PS-PRINT01\HP-Sales-3F and users could not complete normal office printing. The queue itself appeared unhealthy during review, and the issue affected the server-hosted printer path rather than a single workstation. Initial reports were submitted via email to printservices@corplabs.com.
cause: The shared printer queue on PS-PRINT01 had been left in a paused state, preventing queued jobs from processing.
fixed_by: Resume the paused shared printer queues \\PS-PRINT01\HP-Sales-3F and \\PS-PRINT01\HP-HR-2F on PS-PRINT01 using Set-Printer -Name <QueueName> -ComputerName PS-PRINT01 -PrinterStatus Normal, and clear any stale jobs that remained from the paused period (5 orphaned jobs were purged via Remove-PrintJob).

title: Internal DNS names failing to resolve from corporate resolver
description: Internal users and dependent services were unable to reliably reach several corp.local resources, including internal-portal.corp.local and inventory-api.corp.local, because hostname lookups through the corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local, 10.20.1.10) were returning different answers than expected. Reports originated from the Austin office, initially filed by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) after multiple teams noticed intermittent failures reaching internal endpoints by name following a recent infrastructure migration on 2026-05-09. The issue affected service connectivity across multiple internal applications including service-discovery. Workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD belonging to Marcus was among the first clients to surface NXDOMAIN responses. Initial reports suggested a resolver problem, but the current incident required validation of the internal DNS data and resolver path before proceeding.
cause: Outdated A records remained published in the authoritative internal DNS zone for the impacted corp.local hostnames, causing all resolvers to return retired internal addresses.
fixed_by: Update the affected authoritative corp.local zone records on ns1-internal.corp.local and ns2-internal.corp.local so each hostname points to the current internal service address: internal-portal.corp.local → 10.20.50.20, inventory-api.corp.local → 10.20.50.22. Changes applied by Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo).

title: Intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal host 'app-db.internal' from one client subnet
description: Users on the 10.20.30.0/24 internal subnet at the Denver office reported intermittent inability to reach the internal application database host app-db.internal under corp.local, while teams on other networks (e.g., 10.20.40.0/24) reported mixed results. The initial report came from Maria Castillo (emp ID E-20487) who noticed that her workstation WORKSTATION-MC-7741 could not connect to internal services that depend on name resolution. The failure affected access to internal services used by the Internal Apps group, but the reporting context was limited and did not confirm whether the issue was caused by missing DNS data, stale resolver answers, or client path differences. Diagnostics focused on comparing resolver behavior with the authoritative internal DNS service and checking whether cache handling changed the outcome.
cause: Suspected misconfiguration or instability in the corporate resolver path for the internal zone caused intermittent SERVFAIL responses even though the authoritative corp.local records were healthy.
fixed_by: Escalate to the DNS or network infrastructure team (contact: Raj Patel, rpatel, phone 512-555-0173) to review conditional forwarding, recursion behavior, and resolver health for the affected internal zone path on resolver 10.20.30.2 serving the Denver 10.20.30.0/24 subnet.

title: Internal hostname fails to resolve — stale A record in internal DNS
description: Internal users in the Portland office were trying to reach corp.local services by hostname, but some systems continued to fail name resolution even though others reported successful lookups. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40218) via the monitoring-dashboard, noting that her workstation could not resolve app.example.internal or svc-registry.corp.local. The problem affected access to internal endpoints such as service-discovery and application dependencies, with symptoms most visible on clients that had recently changed networks or resumed from long-running sessions. Additional reports came in from developer Raj Patel (raj.patel@corplabs.com) whose machine WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP also failed lookups intermittently. The incident needed DNS validation to determine whether the problem was in the central DNS infrastructure or limited to local resolver behavior on affected systems.
cause: No fault was found in the central internal DNS service; suspected client-side DNS caching, local network settings, or an already-cleared transient issue caused the earlier hostname resolution failures.
fixed_by: Have affected users flush local DNS cache and renew network configuration on impacted endpoints or application hosts. Maria Chen (WORKSTATION-PC-MC, 10.22.47.113) ran ipconfig /flushdns and ipconfig /renew; Raj Patel (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP, 10.22.48.86) reconnected to the Portland office VPN, which refreshed his DNS settings.

title: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed on corporate device
description: A corporate Windows laptop assigned to Marco Pellegrini (employee ID EMP-40291) was still showing as noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune, even though the device appeared to have BitLocker components present locally. The main support concern was that no recovery key was available in the management service for recovery operations. The device hostname is WORKSTATION-SALES-MP and it connects from the Milan office. Marco needed the endpoint to meet corporate encryption compliance, but the current state could not be validated end to end from the available diagnostics.
cause: Recovery key escrow or recovery key visibility in the management service could not be confirmed despite healthy TPM state and successful policy delivery; exact failure point remains unresolved.
fixed_by: Collected BitLocker and MDM logs from WORKSTATION-SALES-MP (hostname confirmed with Marco Pellegrini, EMP-40291) to determine whether recovery key backup attempts were being generated successfully. Logs were exported from C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs and the BitLocker-API event channel.

title: Device marked Noncompliant (missing encryption) — Conditional Access blocks access
description: I (Rachel Nguyen, emp ID EMP-40821) on an Intune-managed Windows device (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-RN) was blocked from accessing Exchange Online because Conditional Access required a compliant device. Company Portal showed the device as Noncompliant after a recent policy review, even though I reported the device had been online and recently synced from the Arlington office. The immediate impact was loss of access to protected Microsoft 365 resources needed for normal work in the Marketing department.
cause: BitLocker/device encryption on the endpoint was suspended or otherwise not in an active protected state, causing the encryption compliance requirement to fail and Conditional Access to block access.
fixed_by: Confirmed local BitLocker status on device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN via remote PowerShell (manage-bde -status C:) and identified that protection was suspended rather than missing due to stale reporting. Agent Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) coordinated with Rachel Nguyen to perform the remediation.

title: Devices marked noncompliant after stale policy reference
description: Marcus Delgado (emp ID: EMP-40291) on an Android 11 device (hostname: WORKSTATION-GALAXY-MD) reported that Outlook and OneDrive were blocked because Conditional Access said the device was not compliant. Company Portal showed a noncompliant encryption-related condition referencing the device compliance policy 'Sales-Mobile-Encryption-v3', but Marcus said he had recently opened Company Portal and believed the device had synced. The issue prevented normal mobile access to business data from the Columbus office, and initial review of the Intune device record (IP: 10.42.88.17) did not immediately show whether the problem was with the device state or policy targeting.
cause: Unable to confirm a single root cause from first-line diagnostics because the available Intune compliance, encryption, and assignment signals were inconsistent.
fixed_by: Collected updated Intune compliance logs, policy assignment details, and Company Portal screenshots from Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com, WORKSTATION-GALAXY-MD) and Rachel Okonkwo (rokonkwo@corplabs.com) to compare device-side encryption status and service-side compliance evaluation state in Endpoint Manager.

title: Users experiencing MFA prompt loop during SSO login (Okta/Azure AD)
description: Several Sales users in the Charlotte office reported they could sign in to the corporate SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) and start access to Salesforce and Workday, but after completing the Okta MFA challenge they were sent back to another MFA prompt instead of reaching the application landing page. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) around 04:30 UTC and confirmed by at least three other team members. The issue appeared after the 04:00 UTC morning identity sync between Azure AD and Okta and blocked normal access to assigned SaaS applications for impacted users in the Sales user group.
cause: A post-sync group membership and application policy assignment mismatch between Azure AD and Okta caused affected users to fall outside the expected access scope during SSO evaluation, resulting in repeated MFA challenges instead of successful session establishment.
fixed_by: Reviewed synced group membership and application assignment for affected Sales users (mdelgado, pnair, kostrowski) across Azure AD and Okta. Confirmed the 'SalesApps-SSO-Access' group membership was present in Azure AD but missing in the Okta mirror after the 04:00 UTC sync.

title: SSO MFA prompt loop for users authenticating via Okta
description: A small group of contractor users reported being unable to complete sign-in through the SSO Portal for Salesforce and Office365. Users including Maria Delgado (mdelgado@externalsales.net) and Raj Patel (rpatel@externalsales.net) stated they were being returned to the MFA screen after approving their Okta Verify challenge, but the behavior was inconsistent and could not be reproduced the same way for every affected account. The issue was first reported by the contractors' onboarding coordinator, Kevin Marsh (EMP-40291), from the Charlotte office. The impact was intermittent access failure for recently onboarded external users in the Sales contractor group.
cause: Suspected incomplete or disabled MFA enrollment on a subset of contractor accounts after identity synchronization, with insufficient evidence to exclude an additional policy evaluation issue.
fixed_by: Reset MFA enrollment for the contractor accounts that showed disabled or incomplete factor state — specifically mdelgado and rpatel — via Okta Admin Console > Directory > People > Reset Multifactor, and require fresh Okta Verify authenticator setup. Also reset lnguyen's enrollment as a precaution given the stale last-verified timestamp.

title: Users experience MFA prompt loop during SSO (Okta/Azure AD)
description: Multiple users reported they could not get through the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) to reach Salesforce, Office365, and other SaaS applications because the sign-in process appeared to return them to MFA repeatedly. The failures started around 2026-05-15 after an identity platform change window (CHG-20260514-0087) that updated federation trust settings between Okta and Azure AD. Affected users include contractors such as Maria Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) and Raj Patel (rpatel@corplabs.com), who reported the issue from the Phoenix office. The problem was observed across different contractor groups provisioned through the new Azure AD sync.
cause: An upstream federated SSO processing fault after MFA completion prevented session establishment and redirected users back to the sign-in flow, creating the appearance of repeated MFA despite valid enrollment and policy scope.
fixed_by: Collected Okta system logs and Azure AD sign-in traces for affected users mdelgado and rpatel showing successful MFA completion (verify_factor: SUCCESS) followed by federation redirect failure with error 'Invalid session state — missing group claim in token'. Traces captured from sessions originating at IPs 10.47.22.118 and 10.47.22.134 in the Phoenix office.

title: Outlook mobile not syncing
description: I was trying to sync email and calendar in Outlook Desktop with my Exchange Online mailbox (rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com), but new items were not updating consistently and mobile access on my iPhone was also unreliable. Outlook connection status was not persistently disconnected — it would flicker between Connected and Disconnected throughout the day — and the problem continued after local client checks, leaving me unable to depend on current mailbox data during the workday. I'm based in the Charlotte office and need reliable sync for client-facing meetings. My employee ID is E-50832 for reference.
cause: Suspected Exchange Online service-side mailbox synchronization issue affecting multiple client sessions, with insufficient local evidence to attribute the failure to the Outlook profile or device compliance.
fixed_by: Documented the inconsistent client sync behavior on both WORKSTATION-RN4417 and IPHONE-RNGUYEN for user rnguyen (rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com) and confirmed that profile rebuild on the desktop did not resolve the mailbox update issue — HTTP 429 throttling persisted across both clients.

title: Outlook shows 'Disconnected' and email not syncing on mobile
description: Outlook mobile on Marcus Delgado's corporate-managed iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) stopped receiving new Exchange Online email around 15:00 UTC and shows a disconnected or stale sync state, while Outlook on his desktop (IP 10.42.17.88) continues to update normally. Marcus (EMP-40291, mdelgado@corplabs.com) needs mobile email access restored because new messages are only appearing on the desktop client. The issue appears limited to the mobile device and there is no indication of a broader mailbox outage affecting the Frankfurt sales team.

description: I am unable to keep Outlook email synchronized on my mobile device (iPhone, hostname MOBILE-IPHONE-MR), where the app shows outdated mailbox content and may briefly appear disconnected. Desktop Outlook access on WORKSTATION-PC-MR is available, indicating I can still reach the mailbox from another client, but mobile email is not updating reliably and is affecting normal responsiveness away from the desk. My employee ID is EMP-209417 and I'm based in the Charlotte office. I have not reported any recent policy prompt or account change on the phone.

title: Outlook not syncing mail on desktop and mobile (Exchange Online)
description: I Outlook stopped syncing new email on both mobile and desktop clients for user Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com), with the mobile app showing stale data and the desktop client intermittently appearing disconnected. The affected mailbox is tied to employee ID EMP-40821 in the Atlanta office, Sales group. I needs normal Outlook access restored because current messages are not reliably updating across devices. No broader Microsoft 365 outage was reported by the user, but the failure is affecting more than one client for the same mailbox. The user's desktop hostname is WORKSTATION-DELL-MD and the iPhone is enrolled via Mobile Device Management.
cause: Likely mailbox-side Exchange Online synchronization fault or service condition affecting multiple clients for a single user, not caused by mobile device compliance or a simple stale local Outlook session.
fixed_by: Collect current Outlook connection state, client logs, and mailbox symptoms from both desktop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MD, IP 10.42.17.88) and mobile to document the cross-client impact for mailbox mdelgado@corplabs.com (EMP-40821, Atlanta office).
